questions.question:
A cube (dice) has six different symbols drawn over its six faces. Three different positions of this cube are shown in the given figure. Which symbol is on the face opposite to ‘*’ (star)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdca9bb9550ddffad00fa5b63a9eb484b4d98f5d81ae64ea3cd58ca3ea625d26.png]
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

From the given three different dices the adjacent sides are as shown below :

As # is common on both the dices I and II, it is clear that %, @, ?, and © are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. * will be opposite to it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c5ac106134c911bcc4712d2824ebc401c5e4d913510be907a442e30ce3d3b21.png] 

Opposite pairs:

% → ©

@ → ?

# → *

So, the opposite side of "*" will be side "#".

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by conclusions numbered 1, 2 and 3. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1. All books are journals.

2. All journals are novels.

3. Some poems are novels.

**Conclusions:**

1. Some novels are books.

2. Some poems are journals.

3. All the journals are books.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef0a1f71150903c9ee4bee538152e9e3abe0eaef07db42678374b50322cbe1af.png] 

Conclusions:

1. Some novels are books → Follow (As all books are journals and all journals are novels. As whole books comes in journals which whole comes in novels, therefore it is true.)

2. Some poems are journals → Does not follow (As all journals are novels and some poems are novels. So it is possible but not definite.)

3. All the journals are books → Does not follow (As all books are journals. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion 1 follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(6, 36, 144)

(9, 81, 324)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number)² = 2nd number; 2nd number × 4 = 3rd number.

Now,

For, (6, 36, 144)

⇒ 6² = 36; 36 × 4 = 144

For, (9, 81, 324)

⇒ 9² = 81; 81 × 4 = 324

Similarly, for** (14, 196, 784)**

**⇒ 14² = 196; 196 × 4 = 784**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**
